chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn al-Husayn, from Amr, from Hasan ibn Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the limit of the worship which, when the performer does it, he would be a performer. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Good intention with the obedience'.
ai.seo_question: What is the essential condition for the validity of worship in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distills the complex jurisprudence of worship into its spiritual core, linking outward obedience (ita'ah) with inward sincerity (husn al-niyyah). This definition underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of form and spirit, where ritual validity is contingent upon the purity of the heart's orientation toward the Divine. It serves as a foundational principle for understanding how external acts are transformed into meaningful worship through conscious devotion.
